thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Canary health-check oscillation detected for release/edgewave v1.2.3 in eu-west-1. Abort criteria: 5xx > 2.5% over 5m AND >2 hosts failing healthchecks. Auto-pager: oncall@redwood (severity: P2)

alex: paging — I’m on it, looking at the canary dashboard. 5xx spike just started ~2m ago.

sam: on call, acknowledged. grabbing logs and health-check traces.

maria: looking at probe-runner, seeing repeated `HTTP/1.1 502` from model-proxy on canary nodes. Probe timeline attached in telemetry.

jade: quick Q — is this regional only? any customers impacted?

alex: initial router metrics show errors concentrated in eu-west-1, small subset of traffic (canary cohort + ~1% of prod due to routing slip). CS pinged.

cs-team: we’ve got 2 inbound tickets from EU customers reporting intermittent 502s for prompt-send. tagging as partial degradation, not yet widespread.

sam: dumping a sample of the failing healthcheck curl:
```
curl -i https://eu-canary-redwood.example/health
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: application/json
{"error":"upstream timeout from model-proxy"}
```

maria: logs from one canary host (node-canary-07):
```
2026-03-15T12:03:12Z model-proxy [warn] connection to runner timed out after 8s
2026-03-15T12:03:13Z runtime [error] failed to allocate kv-cache shard: OOM try=0
2026-03-15T12:03:14Z healthcheck [info] probe failed: status=502
```

alex: interesting — kv-cache OOM + runner timeouts. could be memory pressure with quantized model. We saw a config tweak in the canary: `runtime.kv_cache_size=auto` + `batch_limit=500`.

jade: do we have abort criteria documented? I can flip the kill-switch flag if needed.

sam: current rollout status: 18 hosts total in canary pool, 4 hosts reporting probe failures, 3.1% 5xx across canary traffic in last 5m — meets abort threshold.

alex: performing emergency rollback plan now. Steps I’m taking: 1) toggle feature flag for canary -> OFF, 2) announce pause to routing, 3) start draining canary hosts, 4) kick smoke tests on previous stable.

deploy-bot: Toggle request accepted — `feature.canary_edgewave=false` applied by alex at 2026-03-15T12:06:05Z. Canary rollout paused.

oncall-bot: Handoff note: alex -> jade (in 30m). If regressions continue after rollback, escalate to eng-runtime and open SEV if customer impact expands.

maria: after flag flip, 1m rolling revert of canary routing observed. 5xx rate falling to 0.8% in the last 2m. Healthchecks beginning to stabilize on drained nodes.

sam: drain commands issued to node-canary-* group:
```
kubectl scale --replicas=0 deploy/edgewave-canary -n canary-eu
kubectl cordon node-canary-07 && kubectl drain node-canary-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

cs-team: notifying affected customers: short note in tickets that we detected canary instability and rolled back the canary. ETA for updates: 30m.

alex: mitigation checklist:
- rollback to stable completed ✅
- routing paused ✅
- customers notified ✅
- smoke tests started (running) ⏳
- open follow-up: reproduce locally, check quantization profile + kv-cache sizing, review deploy diff for `batch_limit` bump

jade: taking over oncall. I’ll run the post-rollback health sweep and confirm smoke tests green before we reopen rollout. Also will create a tracking incident for the postmortem.

alex: handing off full context to @jade — logs, probe traces, recent deploy diff in #eng-releases linked. thanks all for quick response. :heart:

jade: ack — I’ll post a short incident summary to #incidents-summary once smoke tests pass. If anything degrades again, page eng-runtime and escalate to SEV.

oncall-bot: Handoff complete: primary oncall = jade (30m). Incident thread will remain open for follow-ups.

sam: one more note — observed transient KV-cache OOM on two hosts. I recommend reverting the aggressive `kv_cache_size=auto` and re-evaluating quantization memory usage before next rollout.

maria: logging follow-ups: capture heap profiles from canary hosts, gather kernel OOM logs, and attach model runner p99 latency to the incident ticket.

jade: noted. I’ll create the follow-up checklist and assign owners. taking over now.

alex: thanks team — closing interim mitigation window. will help on postmortem tomorrow.

cs-team: will keep customers updated. marking impact window: 2026-03-15T12:02 -> 2026-03-15T12:12 (approx).
